assessment_summary.cou_name: Predict head vs flow at 2700 rpm over 3–7 L/min and screen elevated shear volumes to guide blade trim/vane angle for Q4 gate

evidence_keywords: Fluent journal files and meshing scripts are under Git (repo CFD-Pump-RevD, tag v23R2_2024-06-14).
Runs archived in our S3 bucket with containerized environment (Ubuntu 22.04, driver 535.54, Fluent 2023 R2 build 20230628).
Nightly regression on two standard pump cases passed
Two-analyst review used the turbomachinery checklist (REV_7).
Independent read-through by M. Kline (CFD Fellow) on 7/29
manufactured-solution runs on a rotating Couette case recover ~2nd order velocity convergence (slopes 1.95–2.1)
with this Fluent build.
matched the NAFEMS turbomachinery benchmark TM01 within 0.8% head
Three-grid study with poly-hexcore meshes: 3.1M / 8.2M / 17.5M cells; y+ ≈ 0.7 at the finest.
Head at 5 L/min changed by 2.1% (coarse→medium) and 0.9% (medium→fine)
Richardson extrapolation gives an estimated remaining bias of 0.6% on head and 1.3% on torque
Time step for pseudo-transient MRF ramp was 1e−4 s; halving it changed head by <0.2%.
pressure-based coupled solver, second-order spatial and temporal schemes.
residuals <1e−5 and flatlining of head/torque monitors to <0.1% over 500 pseudo-iterations.
No backflow flags or non-orthogonality warnings.
Two-analyst review used the turbomachinery checklist (REV_7).
Are we comparing apples to apples:
Do not extend to pulsatile inlet or off-design speeds without rerunning the checks.
incompressible, isothermal RANS with k–ω SST (+curvature correction). Steady MRF for the rotating region.
Carreau–Yasuda law was used only for the exploratory blood shear postprocessing
Model form check: swapping to realizable k–ε changes head by −1.5% at 5 L/min; DES barely moved head (−0.6%) but increased near-blade shear extremes.
We are holding SST for performance predictions, noting the shear-map caveat.
Working fluid set to match the water–glycerol test mix (μ = 3.5 mPa·s, ρ = 1040 kg/m³).
Tip gaps measured on the Rev C article by CMM (mean 85 μm) informed the nominal; we ran ±30 μm in sensitivity.
inlet total pressure fixed to ambient; outlet mass flow specified per test point; rotor speed 2700 rpm.
Temperature fixed at 25°C (as in the loop).
Comparator: closed-loop water–glycerol bench at 25°C (μ = 3.5 mPa·s). Same Rev D wetted geometry; same speed.
bench dataset BL-0424
CMM report CMM-REV-C-011
Flow meter ±0.5% of reading; differential pressure transducers ±0.25% FS; repeatability 0.8% (1σ).
Temperature control in the loop kept viscosity within ±3% of nominal
No pulsatility in either model or test.
At 3/5/7 L/min, CFD head differed from test
Are we comparing apples to apples:
Flow regime and speed match the loop.
The model includes the same balance-hole leakage paths and vane count.
we mirrored that in the uncertainty bounds.
Agreement: At 3/5/7 L/min, CFD head differed from test by +2.4%, +1.1%, and −1.8%, respectively.
Combined experimental uncertainty on head is ±1.7% (k=2)
Predicted shaft torque is within 3–4% of dynamometer readings
No parameter fitting was done to chase the curve; we only aligned viscosity and speed
